definition_zh: 古董；古物；古老的；古董的
definition_en: an object from an earlier period valued for its age, or an adjective describing such objects
core_image: 旧货店里落着薄尘的黄铜座钟
scene: 街角的小店摆满旧家具，铜器泛着暗光。She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
sceneCN: 这里 antique 是「古董的」（第 2 个义项：形容年代久远且有价值的物品）；句意是她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语 antiquus
形容词：研究古物（收藏）的

senses.title: An object from the past
senses.definition: a piece of furniture, jewellery, or other object that is old and valued for its age
senses.definitionCN: 年代久远、因年代而受珍视的家具、首饰或其他物件
senses.example: She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。
senses.why: Latin antiquus meant 'former, ancient', and the noun use in English picked out objects that survive from that former time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antiquus 意为「从前的、古老的」，英语里的名词用法挑出的就是从那个从前留存下来的物件。

senses.title: Belonging to an earlier period
senses.definition: used of furniture, objects, or styles that come from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 用于来自较早时代的家具、物件或样式
senses.example: The room was full of antique furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆满了古董家具。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain temporal meaning of antiquus, so anything surviving from an earlier age can be called antique.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 antiquus 单纯的时间含义，因此任何从较早年代留存下来的东西都能叫 antique。

senses.title: Old-fashioned, out of date
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way for ideas or methods that belong to the past
senses.definitionCN: 略带嘲意地指属于过去的思想或方法
senses.example: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。
senses.why: Once a thing is old enough to be quaint, the same word can belittle an idea as a museum piece.
senses.whyCN: 当一样东西旧到显得古怪时，同一个词也能把某种观念贬为博物馆里的陈列品。

intro.en: Antique descends from a Latin word for 'former' built on ante, 'before'.
intro.cn: antique 来自拉丁语中表示「从前的」的词，词根是 ante「在前」。

items.en: ante meant 'before' and remains in words such as anterior.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」，仍见于 anterior 等词。

items.en: antiquus meant 'old, former, of long ago'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「旧的、从前的、很久以前的」。

items.en: Old French antique passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 antique 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English first used antique of ancient times and old remains.
items.cn: 英语 antique 最初用于古代与古代遗存。

items.en: By the nineteenth century antique had narrowed to valued old objects and their style.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，antique 已收窄为指受珍视的旧物及其风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for old; the near-meaning group is other words for things from the past.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「旧」的拉丁词根；近义组是其他指旧物的词。

definition_zh: 焦虑；忧虑；担心；渴望
definition_en: an uneasy feeling about something uncertain, a strong wish to do something well, or a medical condition of excessive worry
core_image: 深夜盯着天花板，心里反复盘算明天的事
scene: 考试前一夜，他翻来覆去，脑子里全是没复习到的章节。Her anxiety about the exam kept her awake.
sceneCN: 这里 anxiety 是「焦虑」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事的担忧）；句意是对考试的焦虑让她睡不着。

pos.zh: 名词：焦虑；忧虑；担心；渴望

senses.title: A feeling of worry
senses.definition: an uneasy feeling caused by uncertainty about what may happen
senses.definitionCN: 因不确定将会发生什么而产生的不安
senses.example: Her anxiety about the exam kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 对考试的焦虑让她睡不着。
senses.why: Latin anxietas came from anxius, 'choked, uneasy', which itself came from angere, 'to squeeze or strangle'; anxiety is literally a tightening in the chest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anxietas 来自 anxius「被扼住、不安的」，而 anxius 又来自 angere「挤压、扼住」；所以 anxiety 字面上就是胸口被收紧的感觉。

senses.title: A strong wish to do well
senses.definition: an eager but uneasy wish to please someone or to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 急于讨好某人或把事情做好，却又带着不安的心情
senses.example: He waited with anxiety to hear the judges' decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他急切不安地等着听评委的决定。
senses.why: The same tightening happens when you badly want an outcome, so the word covers eager longing as well as fear.
senses.whyCN: 当你非常想要某个结果时，胸口也会同样收紧，所以这个词既指恐惧也指急切的渴望。

senses.title: A medical condition
senses.definition: a clinical condition marked by persistent and excessive worry
senses.definitionCN: 以持续而过度的担忧为特征的临床病症
senses.example: She was treated for anxiety after months of sleeplessness.
senses.exampleCN: 失眠数月之后，她因焦虑症接受治疗。
senses.why: When the ordinary tightening becomes constant and disabling, the same noun is used as the name of the disorder.
senses.whyCN: 当这种普通的紧绷变得持续且影响生活时，同一个名词就被用来命名这种病症。

intro.en: Anxiety goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to squeeze'.
intro.cn: anxiety 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「挤压」的动词。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze, choke, or torment'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压、使窒息、折磨」。

items.en: anxius described a choked, uneasy state of mind.
items.cn: anxius 形容一种被扼住、不安的心理状态。

items.en: anxietas was the noun for distress and worry.
items.cn: anxietas 是表示痛苦与忧虑的名词。

items.en: English anxiety first meant a troubled, uneasy condition.
items.cn: 英语 anxiety 最初指烦扰不安的状态。

items.en: In the twentieth century anxiety also became the clinical name for a treatable disorder.
items.cn: 二十世纪，anxiety 又成为可治疗的焦虑症的临床名称。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anxious family; the near-meaning group holds other words for unease.
note.cn: 形近组是 anxious 词族；近义组是其他表示不安的词。

definition_zh: 焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried about something uncertain, or very eager to do or get something
core_image: 候诊室里捏皱的挂号单
scene: 手术室外的走廊上，家属一遍遍看墙上的钟。The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anxious 是「焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事感到担忧）；句意是随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。

pos.zh: 形容词：焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的

senses.title: Worried about something
senses.definition: feeling uneasy because you do not know how something will turn out
senses.definitionCN: 因为不知道事情会怎样发展而感到不安
senses.example: The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
senses.exampleCN: 随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。
senses.why: The Latin ancestor angere meant 'to squeeze', and anxius described a person whose chest feels constricted; anxious keeps that bodily tightness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 angere 意为「挤压」，anxius 形容胸口发紧的人；anxious 保留了这种身体上的紧绷感。

senses.title: Very eager to do something
senses.definition: wanting very much to do something or for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常想做某事，或非常希望某事发生
senses.example: She was anxious to finish the report before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她急于在中午前完成报告。
senses.why: Strong desire tightens the mind in much the same way as fear, so anxious for and anxious to express eagerness rather than dread.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的愿望让心里绷紧的方式与恐惧相似，所以 anxious for 与 anxious to 表达的是急切而不是害怕。

intro.en: Anxious is the adjective built on the Latin root for a tightened chest.
intro.cn: anxious 是建立在拉丁语「胸口收紧」词根上的形容词。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze or choke'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压、使窒息」。

items.en: anxius meant 'uneasy, distressed'.

items.en: The noun anxietas named the state of worry.

items.en: English anxious first meant 'greatly troubled'.
items.cn: 英语 anxious 最初意为「极为烦恼的」。

items.en: The sense of eager desire became common in the nineteenth century.

note.cn: 形近组同属拉丁语焦虑词族；近义组是其他表示担忧的词。

normalIntro.en: Anxious is a squeezed chest, whether from fear or from wanting.
normalIntro.cn: anxious 是收紧的胸口，可能因为害怕，也可能因为渴望。

normal.en: Anxious about a problem, anxious to do something.
normal.cn: 对问题用 anxious about，急于做事用 anxious to。

normal.en: The noun is anxiety, not anxiousness in most writing.
normal.cn: 多数书面语中名词用 anxiety，而不用 anxiousness。

normal.en: Anxious for news means waiting eagerly for it.
normal.cn: anxious for news 意为急切等待消息。

normal.en: The x sounds like ks: ANK-shus.
normal.cn: x 读作 ks 的音：ANK-shus。

normal.en: Do not confuse anxious with anger; the root is shared but the meaning is not.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 anger 混为一谈，词根相关但含义不同。

definition_zh: 任何；一些（用于疑问、否定）；丝毫；任何一个
definition_en: one or some, no matter which, used in questions and negatives, or emphasising a small amount
core_image: 一排一模一样的抽屉，随便拉开哪个都行
scene: 冰箱里几乎空了，主人摊开手问客人想喝点什么。Do you have any milk left?
sceneCN: 这里 any 是「一些」（第 1 个义项：用于疑问句中表示不确定的数量）；句意是你还有牛奶吗？

senses.title: Some, in questions and negatives
senses.titleCN: 一些；任何（用于疑问与否定）
senses.definition: an unspecified amount or number, used when asking or denying
senses.definitionCN: 不确定的数量或数目，用于提问或否定
senses.example: Do you have any milk left?
senses.exampleCN: 你还有牛奶吗？
senses.why: Old English ǣnig was literally 'one' with the suffix -ig, so any started as 'a single one' and widened to an unspecified amount.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ǣnig 字面就是「一」加词尾 -ig，因此 any 从「单个一个」扩展为不确定的数量。

senses.title: Whichever one you choose
senses.definition: used to say that one from a group will do, because the choice does not matter
senses.definitionCN: 表示某一组里的任意一个都行，因为选哪个都无所谓
senses.example: Take any seat you like.
senses.exampleCN: 你随便坐哪个座位都行。
senses.why: Once any means 'one, it does not matter which', it naturally expresses free choice among a set.
senses.whyCN: 当 any 表示「随便哪个都行」时，它自然就表达了一组事物中的自由选择。

senses.title: At all, in the least
senses.definition: used with comparatives or negatives to emphasise even a small degree
senses.definitionCN: 与比较级或否定词连用，强调哪怕一点点程度
senses.example: The situation is not any better today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的情况一点也没好转。
senses.why: If even one small amount is in question, the word can stress a minimum degree, which is how the adverb use arose.
senses.whyCN: 如果连很小的量都成问题，这个词就能强调最低程度，副词用法正是这样产生的。

intro.en: Any began as a word for 'one' and slowly loosened into 'some or whichever'.
intro.cn: any 最初表示「一个」，后来逐渐松弛为「一些、随便哪个」。

items.en: ān meant 'one', the ancestor of a, an, and one.
items.cn: ān 意为「一」，是 a、an 与 one 的祖先。

items.en: ǣnig meant 'any one' and was used in questions and negations.
items.cn: ǣnig 意为「任何一个」，用于疑问与否定。

items.en: The form settled as any and spread to all kinds of choice.
items.cn: 形式固定为 any，并扩展到各种选择。

items.en: The adverbial use with comparatives appeared, as in any better.
items.cn: 与比较级连用的副词用法出现，如 any better。

items.en: Any now works as determiner, pronoun, and adverb.
items.cn: 现代 any 兼作限定词、代词与副词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the any- family; the near-meaning group gives other quantity words.
note.cn: 形近组是 any 构成的词族；近义组是其他数量词。

normal.en: Use any in questions and negatives, some in plain statements.
normal.cn: 疑问句与否定句用 any，肯定陈述用 some。

normal.en: Any plus one, thing, body, where builds a whole family.
normal.cn: any 加 one、thing、body、where 构成一整族词。

senses.title: Any person at all
senses.definition: used in questions and negatives to mean one person, it does not matter who
senses.definitionCN: 用于疑问句与否定句，指某个人，是谁都无所谓
senses.example: Anybody can join the club.
senses.exampleCN: 任何人都能加入这个社团。
senses.why: Any supplies 'whichever' and body here is the old word for a person, so anybody is literally 'any person'.
senses.whyCN: any 提供「随便哪个」，body 在这里是古语中「人」的意思，所以 anybody 字面就是「任何一个人」。

senses.title: A person of importance
senses.definition: used in the phrase anybody who is anybody, meaning all the important people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 anybody who is anybody 这一说法，指所有重要人物
senses.example: Anybody who is anybody was at the opening night.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜，所有有头有脸的人都到了。
senses.why: If anybody means every person without exception, then 'anybody who is anybody' narrows it to those who count, giving the ironic sense of a VIP.
senses.whyCN: 既然 anybody 指毫无例外的每个人，那么 anybody who is anybody 就把它收窄为「算得上人物的人」，于是产生了「要人」的讽刺意味。

definition_zh: 无论如何；不管怎样；随便地；杂乱地
definition_en: in spite of what has happened, without a clear plan, or in a careless way
core_image: 断了线的风筝，照样歪歪斜斜地飞着
scene: 车坏在半路，两个人看看彼此，还是决定继续往前走。The road was blocked, but we went anyhow.
sceneCN: 这里 anyhow 是「无论如何」（第 1 个义项：尽管有阻碍仍然如此）；句意是路被堵了，但我们还是往前走。

pos.zh: 副词：无论如何；不管怎样；随便地

derivatives.zh: 副词：无论如何，与 anyhow 基本同义

senses.title: In spite of that
senses.definition: used to say that something happens or is done despite an obstacle
senses.definitionCN: 表示尽管有阻碍，某事仍然发生或被做
senses.example: The road was blocked, but we went anyhow.
senses.exampleCN: 路被堵了，但我们还是往前走。
senses.why: Any supplies 'whichever' and how 'in what manner', so anyhow originally meant 'in any manner at all', and that indifference to the manner grew into indifference to obstacles.
senses.whyCN: any 提供「随便哪个」，how 表示「以何种方式」，所以 anyhow 本义是「以随便哪种方式」，这种对方式的满不在乎就发展成对阻碍的满不在乎。

senses.title: In a careless or random way
senses.definition: in no particular order or with no care
senses.definitionCN: 没有特定次序，也不用心
senses.example: The books were piled anyhow on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 书被胡乱堆在地板上。
senses.why: If any manner will do, the result can look disorderly, which is the older and still living sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 如果随便哪种方式都行，结果就会显得杂乱，这正是这个词较早且仍然存活的义项。

intro.en: Anyhow is the words any and how written as one.

items.cn: 现代它既作连接性副词，也用来形容马虎的摆放。

scene: 会议已经超时，主席看了一眼表，还是决定把最后一项说完。It was late, but she stayed anyway.
sceneCN: 这里 anyway 是「还是；无论如何」（第 1 个义项：尽管有情况仍然如此）；句意是时间很晚了，但她还是留了下来。

pos.zh: 副词：无论如何；不管怎样；而且

senses.title: In spite of that
senses.definition: used when something happens despite a reason against it
senses.definitionCN: 在存在相反理由的情况下某事仍然发生
senses.example: It was late, but she stayed anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 时间很晚了，但她还是留了下来。
senses.why: Any means 'whichever' and way means 'route or manner', so anyway began as 'by any route'; going by any route means going despite obstacles.
senses.whyCN: any 意为「随便哪个」，way 意为「路线或方式」，所以 anyway 本义是「走哪条路都行」；哪条路都走，也就是有阻碍也照走。

senses.title: Adding a further point
senses.definition: used to add a supporting remark or to return to the main topic
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充一个理由，或把话题拉回正题
senses.example: It is too expensive, and anyway we do not need it.
senses.exampleCN: 太贵了，而且我们也不需要它。
senses.why: If the outcome holds by any route, the speaker can add another reason without changing the conclusion, which produces the 'besides' use.
senses.whyCN: 如果无论走哪条路结论都成立，说话人就能再加一个理由而不改变结论，于是产生了「况且」的用法。

senses.title: To change or close a topic
senses.definition: used in speech to signal a return to the subject or the end of a digression

normalIntro.en: Anyway means by any road, so nothing on the road can stop you.

normal.en: Anyway and anyhow are close synonyms.

normal.en: Thanks anyway is the polite close of a refused offer.

normal.en: Use anyway to add a reason: and anyway, it is raining.

normal.en: At the start of a sentence it often closes a digression.

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-y-way.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-y-way。

abstract.en: See a lamp still lit after everyone has left.

definition_zh: 任何地方；无论哪里；随便什么地方
definition_en: in or to any place at all, used in questions, negatives, and general statements
core_image: 一张摊开的世界地图，手指落在哪都行
scene: 年轻人把行李塞进背包，说走就走，没定目的地。We can go anywhere you like.
sceneCN: 这里 anywhere 是「任何地方」（第 1 个义项：不限具体地点）；句意是我们可以去任何你想去的地方。

pos.zh: 副词：任何地方；无论哪里

senses.title: In or to any place
senses.definition: used to refer to a place without saying which one
senses.definitionCN: 指某个地方而不说明是哪一个
senses.example: We can go anywhere you like.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以去任何你想去的地方。
senses.why: Any supplies 'whichever' and where supplies 'place', so anywhere covers the whole map without naming a spot.
senses.whyCN: any 提供「随便哪个」，where 提供「地方」，所以 anywhere 覆盖整张地图却不指名某个地点。

senses.title: At all, in any degree
senses.definition: used in negative sentences to mean not at all, especially with near or close
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句表示「根本不」，常与 near、close 连用
senses.example: The hotel was not anywhere near the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆根本不在海滩附近。
senses.why: If a thing is not in any place near the target, it is not close at all, and that spatial total negation became an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物不在目标附近的任何位置上，那就是完全不远，这种空间上的全盘否定就变成了强调用法。

intro.en: Anywhere is any plus where, a compound of place.

normal.en: Somewhere in statements, anywhere in questions and negatives.

normal.en: Anywhere near means even approximately close.

normal.en: Get anywhere means make progress, often in negatives.
normal.cn: get anywhere 意为有所进展，常用于否定。

normal.en: Anywhere else means any other place than this one.

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-y-where.

dict_mnemonic.text: any（任何）加 where（地方）：任何地方。

root: 由 any「任何」与 where「地方」连写而成，十七世纪固定为副词；与 somewhere、everywhere、nowhere 构成地点系列。

sensesIntro.en: The open place sense can be negated into 'not even close'.
sensesIntro.cn: 开放的「任何地方」义被否定后，就成了「一点也不近」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger free to land on any point of a map.

definition_zh: 分开；相隔；除了；拆散
definition_en: separated by distance or space, into pieces, or not included in something
core_image: 两只原本并排的杯子被推到桌子两端
scene: 吵架之后，两个人一前一后走，中间隔着好几步。They sat apart and said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 apart 是「分开地」（第 1 个义项：彼此隔开一段距离）；句意是他们分开坐着，一言不发。

derivatives.zh: 名词：种族隔离，字面即「分开的状态」
名词：公寓，指分隔出的居住单元
名词：部分，是 apart 的词根

senses.title: Separated by space
senses.definition: at a distance from one another rather than together
senses.definitionCN: 彼此相隔一段距离，而不是在一起
senses.example: They sat apart and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分开坐着，一言不发。
senses.why: The a- here is a worn form of on, and part means a portion, so apart pictures things placed on their own separate portions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 是 on 的弱化形式，part 意为「部分」，所以 apart 描绘的是各自占着一部分、彼此不相连。

senses.title: Into pieces
senses.definition: used with verbs such as take or fall to show something separating into its parts
senses.definitionCN: 与 take、fall 等动词连用，表示事物分成若干部分
senses.example: He took the clock apart to repair it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钟拆开来修理。
senses.why: If the whole is split into its parts, the parts stand apart, so the word moves from distance to dismantling.
senses.whyCN: 如果整体被分成各个部分，这些部分就彼此分开了，于是这个词从「有距离」过渡到「拆解」。

senses.title: Not counting something
senses.definition: used in apart from to mean except for or as well as
senses.definitionCN: 用于 apart from，表示「除了……之外」
senses.example: Apart from the noise, the flat is perfect.
senses.exampleCN: 除了吵一点，这套房子很完美。
senses.why: Something set apart from the rest is left out of the group, which is exactly the logic of 'except'.
senses.whyCN: 被从其余事物中分开的东西就是被排除在外的，这正是「除外」的逻辑。

intro.en: Apart is the phrase on part, meaning 'into separate parts', fused into one word.
intro.cn: apart 由短语 on part「分成各自的部分」融合成词。

items.en: pars meant 'a part or portion', the source of part.
items.cn: pars 意为「部分」，是 part 的来源。

items.en: Old French part carried the word into English.
items.cn: 古法语 part 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: On part meant 'into parts, separately'.
items.cn: on part 意为「分成部分、各自地」。

items.en: The two words fused and the n was lost before the p.
items.cn: 两个词融合，n 在 p 前脱落。

items.en: Apart now covers distance, dismantling, and exception.
items.cn: 现代 apart 涵盖距离、拆解与除外三种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the part root; the near-meaning group gives other words of separation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 part 词根；近义组是其他表示分离的词。

normal.en: Apart from means except for.

normal.en: Fall apart, take apart, tell apart: three verb phrases to learn together.

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（处于）加 part（部分）：各占一部分，就是分开。

root: 由中古英语短语 on part「分成部分」融合而成，part 源于拉丁语 pars「部分」；由「分开」发展出拆解与除外两义。

sensesIntro.en: Being on separate parts gives distance, then dismantling, then exclusion.

senses.title: A set of rooms to live in
senses.definition: a group of rooms used as a home, usually within a larger building
senses.definitionCN: 用作住所的一组房间，通常位于较大的建筑内
senses.example: They rented a small apartment near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近租了一套小公寓。
senses.why: French appartement came from appartement, 'a separation', because the rooms are a portion set apart inside one building.
senses.whyCN: 法语 appartement 来自意为「分隔」的词，因为这套房间就是在一栋楼里被单独分出来的一部分。

senses.title: A room or suite in a large house

definition_zh: 道歉；谢罪；辩白
definition_en: to say that you are sorry for something you have done, or to defend something in speech
core_image: 低着头把一句「对不起」说出口
scene: 他不小心撞翻了别人的咖啡，立刻放下手里的书。She apologized for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 apologize 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：为过错表示歉意）；句意是她为迟到道歉。

senses.title: To say you are sorry
senses.definition: to tell someone that you regret something you did that upset them
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方你为做过并令其不快的事感到抱歉
senses.example: She apologized for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她为迟到道歉。
senses.why: Greek apologia was a speech in defence, built from apo, 'away', and logos, 'word'; the English verb first meant 'to speak in defence' and only later narrowed to owning a fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 apologia 是为自己辩护的言辞，由 apo「离开」与 logos「言辞」构成；英语动词最初意为「出言辩护」，后来才收窄为承认过失。

senses.title: To defend in writing or speech
senses.definition: to argue formally for a belief or a person, a use now mostly found in apologetics
senses.definitionCN: 正式地为某种信念或某人辩护，今多见于护教学语境
senses.example: The essay apologizes for the old custom rather than attacking it.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章是在为旧习俗辩护，而不是抨击它。
senses.why: The older defensive sense survives in apologist and apologetics, where the speaker is explaining a position rather than saying sorry.
senses.whyCN: 较早的辩护义保留在 apologist 与 apologetics 里，那里说话人是在解释一种立场，而不是在道歉。

intro.en: Apologize descends from a Greek word for a speech made in defence.

items.en: English apology first meant a defence, not a confession of fault.
items.cn: 英语 apology 最初指辩护，而非认错。

items.en: The verb apologize shifted to the everyday sense of expressing regret.

definition_zh: 道歉；歉意；辩解；（贫乏的）勉强替代
definition_en: a statement saying you are sorry, a defence of something, or a very poor example of something
core_image: 一封写满「对不起」的短信
scene: 桌上放着一张手写的纸条，第一行就是抱歉的话。He sent a short apology the next day.
sceneCN: 这里 apology 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：为过错表达歉意的话）；句意是他第二天发来一封简短的道歉信。

senses.title: A statement of regret
senses.definition: words saying that you are sorry for something you did

senses.example: He sent a short apology the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他第二天发来一封简短的道歉信。
senses.why: Greek apologia was a speech in defence; English apology kept the 'speech' part and moved from defending oneself to admitting fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 apologia 是辩护的言辞；英语 apology 保留了「言辞」这一部分，并从为自己辩护转为承认过失。

senses.title: A defence of a position
senses.definition: a formal argument in support of a belief, person, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 为某种信念、人物或制度所作的正式论证
senses.example: The book is an apology for classical education.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是为古典教育辩护之作。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense, kept alive in learned writing and in the word apologetics.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义，在学术写作与 apologetics 一词中仍然存活。

senses.title: A very poor example
senses.definition: used in the phrase a poor apology for to mock something that barely deserves the name

senses.example: The hut was a poor apology for a hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 那间小屋勉强算个旅馆。
senses.why: If an apology is words offered in place of a fault, then a poor apology for a thing is a weak substitute standing in for the real one.
senses.whyCN: 如果 apology 是拿来顶替过失的话，那么对某物而言 a poor apology for 就是顶替真货的蹩脚替代品。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的
definition_en: easy to see or understand, or seeming true without being so
core_image: 水面上露出的冰山一角
scene: 会议室的空气一下子僵住，谁都看得出出了问题。It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看出来）；句意是显然出了什么问题。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: Clearly visible or understood
senses.definition: easy to notice or understand from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据证据很容易被察觉或理解
senses.example: It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 显然出了什么问题。
senses.why: Latin apparere meant 'to come into view', built from ad, 'to', and parere, 'to appear'; what is apparent has come into sight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 意为「进入视野」，由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」构成；apparent 就是已经进入视线的东西。

senses.title: Seeming rather than real
senses.definition: true as far as one can see, but possibly not in fact
senses.definitionCN: 就所见而言成立，但事实上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent calm hid a great deal of anger.
senses.exampleCN: 表面上的平静掩藏着极大的愤怒。
senses.why: Because appearing is not the same as being, apparent can warn that the surface may deceive.
senses.whyCN: 因为「显现」不等于「实有」，所以 apparent 可以提醒表面可能欺人。

intro.cn: apparent 来自拉丁语中意为「进入视野」的动词。

normal.en: For no apparent reason means with no visible cause.

normal.en: An apparent heir is the clear legal heir.

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；吸引
definition_en: to make an urgent request, to ask a court to change a decision, or to be attractive to someone
core_image: 人群前举起的一只求助的手
scene: 洪水过后，村长站在废墟前向外界求援。The village appealed for food and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：紧急请求帮助）；句意是村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。

pos.zh: 动词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；有吸引力

senses.title: To ask urgently for help
senses.definition: to ask strongly and publicly for something needed
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地请求所需之物
senses.example: The village appealed for food and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin appellare meant 'to address, call upon', from ad, 'to', and pellere, 'to drive'; an appeal drives words toward someone who can act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appellare 意为「向……讲话、呼唤」，由 ad「向」与 pellere「推动」构成；appeal 就是把话推向能行动的人。

senses.title: To ask a court to reconsider
senses.definition: to take a legal decision to a higher court for review
senses.definitionCN: 把法律裁决提交上级法院复审
senses.example: They appealed against the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对判决提出上诉。
senses.why: The idea of calling upon a higher authority fits the courtroom: the losing side calls on a higher court.
senses.whyCN: 「向更高权威求助」的观念正适用于法庭：败诉一方向更高一级法院发出请求。

senses.title: To be attractive
senses.definition: to please or interest someone, often because it suits their needs
senses.definitionCN: 使人喜欢或感兴趣，常因契合其需要
senses.example: The simple design appeals to young buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 简洁的设计吸引了年轻买家。
senses.why: Something that appeals to you calls out to your taste, so the word moved from a spoken request to a silent attraction.
senses.whyCN: appeal to 你的东西是在向你的品味发出呼唤，所以这个词从口头请求延伸为无声的吸引。

core_image: 舞台幕布拉开，演员走到灯光下
scene: 观众等了几秒，幕布一开，主角从侧幕走出来。A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 appear 是「出现」（第 1 个义项：进入视线）；句意是一个身影出现在走廊尽头。

senses.title: To come into sight
senses.definition: to become visible or present where someone can see you
senses.definitionCN: 变得可见，或出现在别人能看到的地方
senses.example: A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一个身影出现在走廊尽头。
senses.why: Latin apparere joined ad, 'to', and parere, 'to come forth', so appear is a thing stepping into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」合成，所以 appear 就是某物走进视野。

senses.title: To seem a certain way
senses.definition: to give a particular impression, often without being so in fact
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，而事实上未必如此
senses.example: The task appears easier than it is.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务看起来比实际容易。
senses.why: What steps into view is what we judge by, so appear came to mean 'look like' rather than simply 'be present'.
senses.whyCN: 走进视野的东西正是我们判断的依据，所以 appear 从「在场」转为「看起来像」。

senses.title: To be present officially
senses.definition: to attend a court, a hearing, or a public event as required
senses.definitionCN: 按要求出席法庭、听证会或公开活动
senses.example: He must appear before the judge on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 他必须在周一出庭面见法官。
senses.why: A court requires the person to show themselves in the room, which is the plainest form of appearing.
senses.whyCN: 法庭要求当事人亲自出现在庭上，这正是 appear 最朴素的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure stepping out of shadow into light.
core.cn: 核心意象：身影从暗处走入光里。

intro.en: A Latin verb of visibility with a large English family.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示可见的拉丁动词，英语词族庞大。

latinIntro.en: The root parere, 'to appear', underlies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 parere「出现」支撑着整个词族。

definition_zh: 出现；露面；外观；外表
definition_en: the act of coming into sight or being present, or the way someone or something looks
core_image: 镜子前整理衣领的人
scene: 面试前，他对着玻璃门检查自己的衬衫和头发。Her appearance was neat and professional.
sceneCN: 这里 appearance 是「外表」（第 2 个义项：人或物呈现出的样子）；句意是她的外表整洁而专业。

pos.zh: 名词：出现；露面；外观；外表

derivatives.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: The act of appearing
senses.definition: the act of arriving or being seen in public
senses.definitionCN: 到达或在公众场合被看见的行为
senses.example: The singer made a brief appearance on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手在台上短暂露面。
senses.why: The -ance ending turns the verb of coming into view into the event of that coming.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ance 把「进入视野」的动词变成这一事件本身。

senses.title: The way something looks
senses.definition: the visible form or impression that a person or thing gives
senses.definitionCN: 人或物呈现出来的可见形态或给人的印象
senses.example: Her appearance was neat and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的外表整洁而专业。
senses.why: What has appeared is also what we judge by, so the noun shifted from the event to the visible result.
senses.whyCN: 显现出来的东西也是我们判断的依据，于是名词从「事件」转向「可见的结果」。

senses.title: A formal presence in court
senses.definition: the presence of a party before a court or official body
senses.definitionCN: 当事人出现在法庭或官方机构面前
senses.example: His appearance in court lasted only ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的出庭只持续了十分钟。
senses.why: The legal use keeps the plain sense of showing oneself, but fixes it to a required occasion.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留了「亲自现身」的本义，只是把它固定在必须出席的场合。

intro.en: Appearance is the noun made from appear, with the Latin root still visible.
intro.cn: appearance 是由 appear 构成的名词，拉丁词根仍然可见。

items.en: parere meant 'to come forth'.
items.cn: parere 意为「出现」。

items.en: apparere meant 'to become visible'.
items.cn: apparere 意为「显现」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 动词在十三世纪进入英语。

items.en: The noun appearance named the act of coming into sight.
items.cn: 名词 appearance 指进入视野的行为。

items.en: The sense of outward look became the dominant everyday use.
items.cn: 「外观」义成为日常最主要的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the appear root; the near-meaning group gives other words for looks and presence.
note.cn: 形近组共享 appear 词根；近义组是其他表示外观与现身的词。

entries.definition: the act of reaching a place

normalIntro.en: Appearance is both the moment of showing up and the look you show.
normalIntro.cn: appearance 既是露面的那一刻，也是你呈现的样子。

normal.en: Make an appearance means attend briefly.
normal.cn: make an appearance 意为短暂露面。

normal.en: Physical appearance is the common formal phrase for looks.
normal.cn: physical appearance 是「外貌」的正式说法。

normal.en: To all appearances means judging only by the outside.
normal.cn: to all appearances 意为仅从外表判断。

normal.en: The plural appearances often refers to public performances.
normal.cn: 复数 appearances 常指公开演出场次。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPEAR-ance.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPEAR-ance。

abstract.en: See a collar straightened in a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象镜前整理好的衣领。

abstract.en: See a spotlight finding one person.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯找到一个人。

abstract.en: See a name read out in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上被念到的名字。

examples.en: The singer made a brief appearance on stage.
examples.cn: 这位歌手在台上短暂露面。

examples.en: Her appearance was neat and professional.
examples.cn: 她的外表整洁而专业。

examples.en: His appearance in court lasted only ten minutes.
examples.cn: 他的出庭只持续了十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: appear（出现）加 -ance（名词）：出现的样子，外观。

root: 由动词 appear 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；appear 源于拉丁语 apparere「显现」，词根 parere 意为「出现」。

sensesIntro.en: The event of showing up, the look produced by it, and the required court presence.
sensesIntro.cn: 现身的事件、由此产生的外观，以及必须到场的出庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person checked over in a mirror before entering.
core.cn: 核心意象：进门之前在镜前检视自己的人。

intro.en: A regular noun of the appear family, very productive in English.
intro.cn: 这是 appear 词族中的规则名词，在英语中构词力很强。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root parere, 'to appear', runs through the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 parere「出现」贯穿整个词族。

items.meaning: the act of appearing, the look

definition_zh: 附录；阑尾；附件
definition_en: a section of extra material added at the end of a book, or the small tube attached to the intestine
core_image: 书页末尾挂着的一小节补充内容，也像肠子上挂着的一根小尾巴
scene: 论文正文写完了，老师让他把调查问卷放在最后。The questionnaire is in the appendix of her thesis.
sceneCN: 这里 appendix 是「附录」（第 1 个义项：书末的补充材料）；句意是调查问卷放在她论文的附录里。

derivatives.zh: 由 appendix 加表示炎症的 -itis 构成，义为「阑尾炎」
同根动词，义为「附加；贴上」
由 append 加名词后缀构成，义为「附属物；附件」
近义补充词，义为「补充（材料）」

senses.title: A section added at the end of a book
senses.definition: extra information placed at the end of a book or document, such as tables or questionnaires
senses.definitionCN: 放在书或文件末尾的补充信息，如表格、问卷等
senses.example: The full data tables are in the appendix.
senses.exampleCN: 完整的数据表在附录里。
senses.why: The Latin root pendere means to hang; an appendix is material that hangs at the end of the main text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pendere 意为「悬挂」；附录就是挂在正文末尾的材料。

senses.title: The tube attached to the intestine
senses.definition: the small closed tube joined to the beginning of the large intestine
senses.definitionCN: 连接在大肠起始处的一根封闭小管
senses.example: Doctors removed her inflamed appendix.
senses.exampleCN: 医生切除了她发炎的阑尾。
senses.why: The organ is also something that hangs off a larger part, so anatomy borrowed the same hanging image.
senses.whyCN: 这个器官同样是从较大部位上「垂挂」下来的东西，解剖学借用了同一个悬挂意象。

senses.title: A body part joined to a main structure
senses.definition: a smaller or less important part attached to a larger body or structure
senses.definitionCN: 附属于较大身体或结构的较小部分
senses.example: The tail is an important appendix in many animals.
senses.exampleCN: 尾巴是许多动物重要的附属部分。
senses.why: When something merely hangs on the outside of a structure, English reuses this word for it.
senses.whyCN: 当某物只是挂附在结构外部时，英语就复用这个词来称呼它。

intro.en: Appendix is Latin for 'something that hangs on', applied to book material and to an organ.
intro.cn: appendix 是拉丁语「挂附之物」，既用于书籍材料，也用于一个器官。

items.en: The reconstructed root *(s)pen- is generally taken to mean 'to draw, hang'.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *(s)pen- 表示「拉、悬挂」。

items.en: appendere meant to hang something on; appendix was the noun of result.
items.cn: appendere 意为把东西挂上去；appendix 是其结果名词。

items.en: appendix already meant an addition to a text.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 appendix 已指文本的附加部分。

items.en: English borrowed it for book appendices.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该词，指书末附录。

items.en: Anatomy applied the same word to the intestinal tube.
items.cn: 十七世纪解剖学把同一词用于肠上的小管。

items.en: Both the book sense and the organ sense are common today.
items.cn: 今天书附录义与器官义都很常用。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pend- hanging family; the near-meaning group gathers other add-on material.
note.cn: 形近组是 pend-「悬挂」词族；近义组是其他附加材料。

entries.definition: to add something at the end
a part joined to something larger
material added to complete or extend a text
a file or item joined to a main one
an addition to a document or building

normalIntro.en: An appendix hangs at the end, like a tag on a book.
normalIntro.cn: appendix 挂在末尾，像书后面挂着的标签。

normal.en: Append means to attach at the end; an appendix is what you append.
normal.cn: append 是附加，appendix 是附加出来的东西。

normal.en: Academic papers use the plural appendices.
normal.cn: 学术论文常用复数 appendices。

normal.en: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
normal.cn: appendicitis 是阑尾发炎，即阑尾炎。

normal.en: Refer to the appendix for the full data.
normal.cn: 完整数据参见附录，是论文常用说法。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PEN-dix.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节：a-PEN-dix。

abstract.en: See a small pouch hanging at the end of a thick book.
abstract.cn: 想象厚书末尾挂着的小册子。

abstract.en: See a tiny tail hanging inside the body.
abstract.cn: 想象体内垂着的一根小尾巴。

abstract.en: See extra pages swinging behind the main text.
abstract.cn: 想象正文后摆动的附加页。

examples.en: The questionnaire is in the appendix of her thesis.
examples.cn: 调查问卷放在她论文的附录里。

examples.en: The full data tables are in the appendix.
examples.cn: 完整的数据表在附录里。

examples.en: Doctors removed her inflamed appendix.
examples.cn: 医生切除了她发炎的阑尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俄喷的」——像俄然喷出挂在书后的一截附加内容，附录。

root: 来自拉丁语 appendix「挂附之物」，由 appendere「挂上去」（ap- 去 + pendere 悬挂）派生；书末附录与体内阑尾都是「挂附」意象。

sensesIntro.en: One hanging image splits into extra pages at the end of a book and a small tube hanging in the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「悬挂」意象分成书末的附加材料和体内垂挂的小管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that hangs at the end of a larger whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在更大整体末尾的东西。

intro.en: A Latin hanging-family noun whose root also gives pend and suspend.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁「悬挂」词族的名词，同根词还有 pend 与 suspend。

latinIntro.en: Latin appendere combines ad- (towards) and pendere (to hang).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 appendere 由 ad-（朝向）与 pendere（悬挂）构成。

definition_zh: 食欲；胃口；欲望；兴趣
definition_en: a natural desire for food, or a strong interest in something
core_image: 闻到厨房香味时咽下的口水
scene: 锅盖一掀，热气冲上脸，他立刻觉得饿了。The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
sceneCN: 这里 appetite 是「食欲」（第 1 个义项：对食物的自然欲望）；句意是面包的香味让他有了食欲。

senses.title: A desire for food
senses.definition: the natural feeling that makes you want to eat
senses.definitionCN: 使人想吃东西的自然感觉
senses.example: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。
senses.why: Latin appetitus came from appetere, 'to seek after', built from ad, 'to', and petere, 'to seek'; hunger is the body seeking food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appetitus 来自 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；饥饿就是身体在追寻食物。

senses.title: A strong interest in something
senses.definition: a keen desire for an activity, a challenge, or a type of experience
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、挑战或某种体验的强烈渴望
senses.example: She has an appetite for risk.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢冒险。
senses.why: The seeking after food widened to any object the mind reaches for, so appetite can name ambition or curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 对食物的追寻扩展到心里想抓取的任何对象，所以 appetite 也能指抱负或好奇心。

intro.en: Appetite goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to seek after'.
intro.cn: appetite 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「追寻」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: petere meant 'to seek, aim at'.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、瞄准」。

items.en: appetere meant 'to reach for, desire'.
items.cn: appetere 意为「伸手去取、渴望」。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The figurative sense of desiring challenges or knowledge became common.
items.cn: 渴望挑战或知识的比喻义变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the seek root; the near-meaning group gives other words for desire.
note.cn: 形近组共享「寻求」词根；近义组是其他表示欲望的词。

a contest, from the same seeking verb

normalIntro.en: Appetite is the body or mind reaching out for something.
normalIntro.cn: appetite 就是身体或心思向外伸出去抓某样东西。

normal.en: Lose one's appetite and a good appetite are opposite fixed pairs.
normal.cn: lose one's appetite 与 a good appetite 是相反的两个固定搭配。

normal.en: An appetite for risk means a taste for it.
normal.cn: an appetite for risk 意为喜欢冒险。

normal.en: Whet one's appetite means make someone want more.
normal.cn: whet one's appetite 意为吊起胃口。

normal.en: Appetizer is the small dish that starts a meal.
normal.cn: appetizer 是开胃的头盘。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AP-pe-tite.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AP-pe-tite。

abstract.en: See steam rising from a covered pot.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖下冒出的热气。

abstract.en: See a hand reach toward a bread basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向面包篮。

abstract.en: See a climber eyeing a high wall.
abstract.cn: 想象攀爬者盯着高墙。

examples.en: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
examples.cn: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。

examples.en: She has an appetite for risk.
examples.cn: 她喜欢冒险。

examples.en: He lost his appetite after the long journey.
examples.cn: 长途旅行之后他没了胃口。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 pet（寻求）加 -ite：向食物伸出去的欲望，食欲。

root: 来自拉丁语 appetitus，源于 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；同根词有 appetizing、appetizer，另有 compete、petition。

sensesIntro.en: Seeking food and seeking experience are the same reaching motion.
sensesIntro.cn: 追寻食物与追寻体验，是同一个向外伸手的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving toward food before the mind decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在脑子决定之前已伸向食物。

intro.en: A Latin noun of seeking that English applies to food and to ambition.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示追寻的拉丁名词，英语中兼指食物与抱负。

latinIntro.en: The root petere, 'to seek', also gives petition and compete.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 petere「寻求」也派生出 petition 与 compete。
